methods.label: Check the reciprocals
methods.explanation:
The reciprocal of a nonzero number \(n\) is \(1/n\). For \(-2\), the reciprocal is \(-1/2\), and
\[
-2<-\frac12.
\]
This inequality holds because \(-2\) lies farther left on the number line. The numbers \(-1\) and \(1\) equal their reciprocals, while \(2>1/2\). Zero has no reciprocal because multiplying zero by any number gives zero, never one. Thus the only qualifying number is \(-2\), choice A.
